verses.1: Sarai, Abram's wife, had not been able to have children. She had an Egyptian servant named Hagar.
verses.2: Sarai said to Abram, "The LORD has kept me from having children. Go and sleep with my servant Hagar. Perhaps I can have a family through her." Abram agreed and listened to Sarai.
verses.3: After Abram had been living in the land of Canaan for ten years, Sarai took her servant Hagar and gave her to Abram as a wife.
verses.4: Abram slept with Hagar, and she became pregnant. When Hagar realized she was pregnant, she began to look down on her mistress Sarai.
verses.5: Sarai said to Abram, "This is your fault! I gave you my servant, and now that she is pregnant she treats me with disrespect. May the LORD judge between us."
verses.6: Abram said to Sarai, "She is your servant. Do with her whatever you think is right." Then Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that Hagar ran away.
verses.7: The angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring of water in the wilderness, near the spring on the road to Shur.
verses.8: The angel said, "Hagar, servant of Sarai, where have you come from and where are you going?" She answered, "I am running away from my mistress Sarai."
verses.9: The angel of the LORD told her, "Go back to your mistress and submit to her authority."
verses.10: The angel of the LORD also said, "I will give you so many descendants that no one will be able to count them all."
verses.11: Then the angel of the LORD said, "You are pregnant and will give birth to a son. You are to name him Ishmael, because the LORD has heard your suffering.
verses.12: He will be like a wild donkey of a man. He will fight against many people, and many people will fight against him. He will live apart from his relatives."
verses.13: Hagar gave a name to the LORD who had spoken to her. She said, "You are the God who sees me." She said this because she thought, "Have I really seen the One who watches over me?"
verses.14: That is why the well was named Beer-lahai-roi. It is located between Kadesh and Bered.
verses.15: Hagar gave birth to a son for Abram, and Abram named him Ishmael.
verses.16: Abram was 86 years old when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael.

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
